speccheck.paper: Chalkias, Garillot, Nikolaenko, 'Taming the many EdDSAs', SSR 2020, https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1244
speccheck.verdicts: README 'Results' table of the same repository: 'Dalek strict' row for strict, 'Zebra' row (the ZIP-215 reference implementation) for zip215. rfc8032Cofactored is the 'cof-ed' column of the README condition table combined with the RFC 8032 checks S < L and canonical point encodings (cases 6 to 11 rejected).

cctv.selection: The first vector (lowest number) of each distinct flag set: 66 of 914 vectors, verbatim.
cctv.strictRule: ed25519-dalek tests/validation_criteria.rs: verify_strict() succeeds if and only if the flags are a subset of {low_order_component_A, low_order_component_R}.
cctv.zip215Rule: CCTV README: ZIP-215 rules accept every vector, except that reencoded_k vectors compute k from the canonical encoding, which ZIP-215 does not do (it hashes the bytes as given).

_source.msgEncoding: speccheck messages are hex; CCTV messages are UTF-8 strings

dalekNonCanonicalKeys.origin: Cases generated during the internal review of 2026-11-11: non-canonical encodings of the public key A for mixed-order points, each with the verdict of ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 verify_strict.
dalekNonCanonicalKeys.oracle: ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 with curve25519-dalek 4.1.3, the exact path of soroban-env-host 29.0.1: VerifyingKey::from_bytes then verify_strict.
dalekNonCanonicalKeys.keys: The 20 encodings y = p + c, c in {3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 14, 15, 16, 18}, sign bit 0 or 1: non-canonical encodings of points of order 2L, 4L or 8L (not of small order). dalek decodes all of them.
dalekNonCanonicalKeys.cases: 4 signatures per key from the review corpus (3 random, 1 honest signature by another key), with the host verdicts: key decodes, signature rejected.
